statement: Let D be the set of decimal digits represented by digits: D = { d in {1,...,9} | there exists i with 0 <= i < len(digits) and digits[i][0] = 48 + d }. The function returns a result r (it does not fail) and r is exactly the number of positive integers m with 1 <= m <= n whose ordinary decimal representation (base 10, without leading zeros) has every digit in D.
preconditions: 1 <= len(digits) <= 9; for every i with 0 <= i < len(digits), len(digits[i]) = 1 and 49 <= digits[i][0] <= 57; the byte values digits[i][0] are pairwise distinct and non-decreasing in i; 1 <= n <= 1000000000.

Whenever the function returns a result r, let L be the number of decimal digits of n, so 10^(L-1) <= n <= 10^L - 1. Then r = (sum_{k=1}^{L-1} |D|^k) + B, where B is the number of integers m with 10^(L-1) <= m <= n whose decimal representation uses only digits in D.
